title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline (gpt-5-mini generation + deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) run against a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator. To control model-call budget we used a shared-initial-generation protocol: a single LLM candidate per intent was produced and then (A) accepted as the ungated baseline and (B) validated and repaired (if needed) in the guarded arm. This design makes the primary estimand a repair-on-same-candidate effect rather than a comparison of independently re-sampled generation pipelines. Key outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.015]. Observed operational counts from the archived execution: initial validator failures (validation_before.valid == false) = 1, syntactic/parse failures = 0, deterministic repair invocations = 1, provider/API failures = 0, hosted-model calls used = 201. The preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect is excluded by the CI. We report these artifact-grounded facts, provide a concise description of the deterministic validator used, and discuss interpretive limits (shared-generation estimand, synthetic task set, single LLM, bounded repair budget, emulator fidelity).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configuration and generating repair actions. However, LLM outputs can be syntactically plausible yet operationally incorrect (hallucinations, missing required steps, ordering errors), posing safety risks in network change workflows. Prior work therefore recommends pairing LLMs with deterministic validators, constrained decoding, or iterative repair loops. We designed a narrowly scoped, preregistered, autonomy-locked paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard increases the proportion of emulator-executable configurations produced from natural-language NetOps intents compared with ungated LLM generation. Our contribution is (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), (2) full execution and analysis artifacts, and (3) the quantitative confirmatory result and its practical interpretation under the shared-initial-generation protocol.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps prototypes, surveys, and intent-translation studies document active research on intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilots while reporting hallucination and schema-violation failures [Nguyen et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025]. Mitigation strategies from adjacent domains include retrieval-augmented generation, live schema grounding, constrained decoding, and verifier-augmented generate–validate–repair pipelines; these reduce but do not eliminate incorrect outputs. Formal verification formalisms and ensemble verifiers (NetKAT variants, weighted NetKAT, ensemble checkers) can detect reachability/isolation violations and are natural validators, although they face control-plane-fidelity and scalability issues. Our experiment targets the concrete question of repair efficacy on identical LLM candidates under a strict, preregistered paired design and therefore complements prior architectural and mitigation studies.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered a single primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory set: n=200 paired natural-language intents curated to span small single- and multi-device changes (ACLs, interface MTU/VLAN changes, uplink switchover patterns). Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator, deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, orchestration adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Model: gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) as declared in execution/model_configuration.json. Model-call budget constrained maximum hosted-model calls to 400; to respect this budget we used a shared-initial-generation protocol: one shared initial candidate per intent (shared_initial_generation) was produced and used by both arms. Baseline: accept the shared candidate as the ungated output. Guarded: run deterministic validation on the same shared candidate and, if the validator reported violations, invoke up to one deterministic repair iteration (preregistered repair budget ≤1). Success endpoint: an episode is successful when validator validation_after.valid == true after applying the generated (or repaired) configuration to the emulator. Analysis: primary test = exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary success/failure; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). Missingness, retry, and contamination rules were preregistered and followed.
sections.results: Execution and artifact accounting: the run completed 400 episodes (200 paired intents) with no provider/API errors; hosted-model calls used = 201 (≤ planned 400). Provider-call accounting shows stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1. Primary outcomes (artifact-backed): baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11 = 199, n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 (two-sided exact test on discordant counts n10=1, n01=0). Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.015]. Artifact-grounded operational counts (from execution/* and analysis/*): initial validator failures (validation_before.valid == false) = 1; syntactic/parse failures = 0; deterministic repair invocations = 1; provider/API failures = 0; hosted-model calls used = 201. Secondary planned analyses (failure-taxonomy, repair-iteration yield) were limited because the confirmatory set produced only a single repair invocation and therefore provided minimal discordant information for subgroup inference. Per-episode prompts, responses, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis CSVs are archived (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: In this preregistered, emulator-grounded setting for the curated synthetic intent family, ungated gpt-5-mini generation already produced near-perfect emulator-executable configurations and the bounded GVR guard yielded a small absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points). The paired 95% CI excludes the preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect, so the confirmatory hypothesis that a bounded GVR guard would provide a substantial gain in this exact setup is not supported. Crucially, the shared-initial-generation protocol (preregistered) isolates the deterministic validator/repair operator's ability to correct an identical LLM-produced candidate: the estimand is therefore "repair efficacy on the same candidate" rather than the operational comparison of two independently sampled pipelines (which would allow the guarded arm to resample a different—possibly correct—candidate). Practical implication: a small or null observed guarded gain under this estimand can arise either because the LLM rarely produced repairable defects under the confirmatory distribution (observed here) or because a guard that allowed independent re-generation might yield larger gains at higher model-call cost. Threats to validity: curated synthetic task set, single LLM (gpt-5-mini), single emulator, single deterministic validator implementation, bounded repair budget (≤1), and the shared-generation protocol all limit external generalizability. Reproducibility: all artifacts, prompts, and analysis code are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
sections.conclusion: We ran an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to evaluate a bounded generate–verify–repair guard on gpt-5-mini across 200 curated NetOps intents. Ungated generation succeeded in 199/200 cases; the guarded GVR pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]). These artifact-backed results show that the marginal repair-on-same-candidate effect was negligible under this confirmatory distribution and bounded protocol. This does not contradict prior work that finds GVR value in harder, adversarial, or independent-generation comparisons; rather, it highlights that guard utility depends strongly on task difficulty, model capability, emulator fidelity, and estimand design (shared-initial vs independent resampling). Future work should evaluate independent-generation comparisons, multivendor CLIs, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and operational axes such as verification latency and rollback cost.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to (i) selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and (ii) approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary; no manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) as declared in execution/model_configuration.json; deterministic validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule appear in execution/scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample size n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting: the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; the guarded pipeline invoked the deterministic repair stage exactly once (provider-call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm. The primary estimand should therefore be read as repair-on-same-candidate efficacy.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Aggregate task-difficulty counts (easy / medium / hard / very_hard) for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) but were not summarized into tabular counts in this manuscript due to the compact presentation; readers may inspect execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle for per-task difficulty metadata.
